source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-93: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 93 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume RoCE is the intended transport, but verify this rather than infer it from the application label. Verify GPU/NIC PCIe/NVLink affinity, GPU-direct versus host staging, software and firmware versions, link speed, MTU, VLAN/priority mapping, PFC/ECN, route symmetry, queue pairs, memory registration, selected transport and any fallback, message sizes, concurrency, placement, and clocks. A falsifiable hypothesis is that congestion or an asymmetric route in the relevant priority class increases p99.9 while the median, workload, and placement remain stable; host scheduling, CPU contention, and workload drift are competing explanations. Capture synchronized application and verbs/completion timings together with NIC retries, errors, drops and ECN, plus switch queue depth and PFC pause counters where available. Measure p50, p95, p99 and p99.9 latency in ms, throughput, completion errors, retries and timeouts over equal-size interleaved baseline and treatment samples; report sample counts, workload parameters and uncertainty, not just a mean or one run. Preserve and redact evidence, and do not claim causality without a matched comparison. Any configuration change requires owner authorization, a saved known-good state, one-variable canary, correctness validation, and explicit rollback on preset tail-latency, timeout, drop/pause, completion-error, or correctness thresholds.
